title: Stochastic prefetch credit accounting sketch
content:
Purpose
---
Quick brain-dump / sketch for a credit-based accounting system that enables stochastic prefetching from the client/proxy while keeping overall token-cost predictable and fair across tenants. Goal: let clients prefetch some work to reduce tail latency, but bound the economic exposure and make backpressure tractable.

Problem statement
---
- Prefetch increases perceived latency and hit-rate for caches, but it costs tokens and compute.
- Different tenants and clients have different risk tolerances.
- We want a decentralized-ish protocol (client-side prefetch heuristics + ingress accounting) that:
  1) Caps expected spend from prefetching per tenant (and optionally per-client).
  2) Allows stochastic prefetching (sampled) to improve tail without linear cost growth.
  3) Provides transparent metrics to owner teams so they can tune.

Key constraints/assumptions
---
- We operate in two places: client/proxy (makes prefetch decisions) and ingress/serving runtime (authoritative charge & reconciliation).
- Prefetch tokens are billed when work executes on the model runtime. Clients should be able to *reserve* credits locally and spend them; ingress must reconcile to avoid freeloading.
- Latency SLOs matter: prefetch decisions must be fast and low-overhead.
- Must play nicely with existing batching + KV cache semantics.

High-level design idea
---
- Each tenant gets a periodic credit allocation for prefetching (configurable: tokens/day, tokens/minute). Credits represent authorization to run extra speculative tokens beyond the baseline request cost.
- Clients request a *prefetch ticket* (lightweight signed token) from a control plane endpoint; ticket carries: tenant_id, ticket_id, allowed_token_budget, expiry_ts, sampling_rate, and a short HMAC.
- Clients may also run purely local stochastic heuristics (no ticket) but such prefetches are treated as "uncredited" and billed to the tenant immediately at full rate and flagged for higher sampling in audits. Prefer tickets.

Ticket lifecycle (sketch)
---
1) Client asks control plane: "give ticket with B tokens and TTL T".
   - Control plane enforces tenant-level token caps and issuance rate.
2) Client uses ticket to issue prefetch request(s) to ingress with metadata: ticket_id, claimed_tokens_for_this_call (t), sample_seed.
3) Ingress verifies ticket HMAC & expiry, then temporarily apply a soft hold of t tokens from tenant's running balance (not final charge yet). If hold would exceed tenant cap, ingress either reject or downgrade request.
4) When prefetch executes on runtime, actual consumed tokens (real_t) are recorded. Final charge = min(real_t, t) or optionally allow small overage bucket with different rate. Release unused hold back to tenant balance.

Stochastic sampling integration
---
- Ticket can encode a sampling_rate p (0..1). If client wants to prefetch n candidate completions but only wants to run k expected, client can use sampling to only materialize ~p*n.
- sampling pseudo-algo: draw u ~ Uniform(0,1); if u < p then call runtime; else skip. To ensure statistical guarantees across many clients, maintain per-ticket RNG seed and nonce to avoid correlated bursts.

Accounting semantics and fairness
---
- Allocation model: credits are soft tokens that expire (e.g., per-minute sliding window). Two accounting counters maintained per tenant: issued_credits and consumed_tokens. An ingress-side reconciler periodically enforces issued_credits >= consumed_tokens.
- If consumed_tokens > issued_credits (client over-spend / race), create a compensating charge event to tenant billing and optionally throttle subsequent tickets.
- Prefer additive smoothing: track rolling 1m/1h/1d consumption to support both burst and sustained limits.

Economics and pricing levers
---
- Prefetch discount factor: prefetch tokens could be billed at a premium (e.g., 1.2x normal) to discourage wasteful speculation by default, or at a discount if it demonstrably reduces cost elsewhere (e.g., fewer cold-starts).
- Overage policy: small overages (<= 10% per ticket) allowed and billed at 1.0x; large overages bill at 1.5x and trigger ticket revocation.
- Refund policy: if a prefetch was never consumed (ticket expired without use), simply expire credits (no refund) to simplify bookkeeping. Optional manual refunds via ops for edge cases.

Telemetry and observability
---
- Emit events: ticket_issued, ticket_used(preflight + final_charge), ticket_rejected, ticket_revoked, overage_alert.
- Per-tenant dashboards: prefetch tokens issued, consumed, success-rate (prefetch -> actual useful hit as defined by team), average token-per-prefetch, tail-latency improvement estimate.
- Light-weight audit sample: store 1% of prefetch inputs+outputs (masked) for quality checks.

Protocol examples and edge cases
---
Example POST from client to control-plane to request ticket (pseudo):
POST /v1/prefetch/tickets { tenant: T, wanted_budget: 500, ttl_s: 60 } -> returns ticket blob w/ hmac

Client uses ticket to make prefetching call:
POST /generate?prefetch_ticket=xxx { prompt: "...", claimed_tokens: 40, nonce: 3453 }
Ingress verifies ticket and decrements pending balance by 40.

Edge cases:
- Lost or duplicated calls: ingress must be idempotent on ticket+nonce to avoid double holds. Nonce window per ticket.
- Oversubscription across distributed edge proxies: centralized control-plane + local caching of a small number of tickets per client avoids roundtrip for every prefetch ticket request. Tickets short-lived so misuse window limited.
- Clients offline: cannot request new tickets; old tickets expire.

Algorithm sketch for ticket issuance quota
---
- Each tenant has max_rate R tokens/sec and burst_capacity B.
- Control-plane maintains a token-bucket per tenant, refilled at R. When client requests wanted_budget W, if W <= tokens_in_bucket + B then issue up to min(W, tokens_in_bucket + B) and decrement bucket. Otherwise issue reduced ticket or reject.
- To support stochastic sampling, prefer issuing smaller tickets with higher sample rates rather than one huge ticket (gives better multiplexing and audit properties).

Safety knobs for runtime stability
---
- Ingress global kill-switch: if total prefetch load threatens runtime SLOs, ingress can blackhole prefetch tickets (return 503 + try-later) and mark a flag in ticket responses indicating backoff.
- Per-tenant backpressure: if tenant consumes > threshold of CPU/GPU, downgrade their ticket issuance rate automatically.

Open questions / TODOs
---
- Where do cached KV prefetch hits attribute their savings? If a prefetch avoids a later higher-cost request, how to reflect that in tenant-level accounting? (short answer: need attribution heuristics; record correlation windows and credit-back some tokens as a negative charge?)
- How to measure "usefulness" of a prefetch objectively? Sampling + offline evals probably needed.
- Do we want client-side adaptive learning to tune sampling_rate p per ticket based on observed hit-rate? Probably yes, but need safety.
- UX: expose a simple CLI/SDK helper to request/refresh tickets and surface remaining prefetch budget to devs.

Notes for next iteration
---
- Draw state diagram for ticket lifecycle, idempotency window and hold-vs-final-charge flow.
- Simulate micro-economics with synthetic tenants (vary hit-rates, burstiness) to tune discount factors and overage policies.
- Prototype short-lived ticket API + ingress hold flow in a canary region.

Quick ascii diagram (very rough)
---
[client] --(ticket request)--> [control-plane] --(ticket)--> [client]
[client] --(prefetch w/ ticket)--> [ingress] --(hold)--> [tenant balance]
[runtime] --(exec & report usage)--> [ingress reconciler] --(finalize charge)--> [billing system]

Random brain-dump of heuristics for client agent (local)
---
- Maintain last N prompts + hit outcome; compute empirical P(useful|prefetch) and p_tune = min(0.5, baseline_p * sqrt(hitrate)).
- Prefer small speculative lengths (e.g., 32 tokens) unless context suggests larger is valuable.
- If ticket budget low, reduce p by half and increase only when consecutive hits > 3.

End notes
---
This is intentionally rough. Want to iterate with Priya/Connor on: ticket shape, reconciliation window, and pricing multipliers. Next step: lightweight sim + minimal API prototype.
